FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Cytogenetics and Molecular Pathology

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
Age/Sex: 63-year-old male
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peri-renal mass biopsy
Clinical Diagnosis: Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma (DLBCL)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Analysis of peri-renal mass biopsy from patient with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma to assess for genetic rearrangements associated with high-grade B-cell NHL.

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using the following probe sets:
• IGH/MYC/CEP 8 Tri-Color Dual Fusion Translocation Probe (Abbott Molecular)
• IGH/BCL2 Dual Color Dual Fusion Translocation Probe (Abbott Molecular)
• BCL6 Dual Color Break Apart Rearrangement Probe (Abbott Molecular)
• MYC Break Apart Rearrangement Probe (Abbott Molecular)

Analysis was correlated with CD79a immunostain to identify B-cell populations. A minimum of 100 interphase nuclei were examined for each probe set.

RESULTS

1. MYC (8q24) Rearrangement Analysis:
   - MYC Break Apart: POSITIVE for rearrangement
   - IGH-MYC t(8;14) Fusion: NEGATIVE
   - Abnormal signal pattern: 1F1O1G (78/100 cells)
   - Interpretation: MYC rearrangement present with non-IGH partner

2. IGH-BCL2 t(14;18) Analysis:
   - Result: POSITIVE for IGH-BCL2 fusion
   - Abnormal signal pattern: 1F1O1G1R (82/100 cells)
   - Interpretation: Presence of t(14;18)(q32;q21) rearrangement

3. BCL6 (3q27) Rearrangement Analysis:
   - Result: POSITIVE for rearrangement
   - Abnormal signal pattern: 1F1O1G (75/100 cells)
   - Interpretation: BCL6 gene rearrangement detected

4. CEP 8 Analysis:
   - Result: Normal diploid pattern (2 signals)

INTERPRETATION
This FISH analysis reveals an abnormal result with triple concurrent rearrangements:
• MYC rearrangement without IGH-MYC fusion (non-IG partner)
• IGH-BCL2 fusion [t(14;18)]
• BCL6 rearrangement

This rare genetic profile of concurrent MYC, IGH-BCL2, and BCL6 rearrangements in high-grade B-cell NHL is typically associated with poor prognosis. The presence of MYC rearrangement with a non-immunoglobulin partner, combined with BCL2 and BCL6 alterations, represents a complex karyotype that may influence therapeutic decisions and clinical outcomes.

The findings should be correlated with morphologic, immunophenotypic, and clinical features for comprehensive patient management.

Reported by: [redacted name], Ph.D., FACMG
Reviewed by: [redacted name], M.D., Ph.D.
